A-access-permissions-modular-typestate-2.relevance-description: The paper that prices MODULARITY, which is the question 28Q faces in deciding how much an oracle must declare. Three concrete costs. (1) Aliasing is not binary: a five-way taxonomy over two independent axes — what THIS reference may do and what OTHERS may do — which is the right vocabulary for 'we hold the only session', 'we mutate but a monitoring agent reads', and 'we read while something may write'. (2) Weak permissions get only TEMPORARY state knowledge, discarded after any effectful expression because the object may have changed without this reference's knowledge — the precise formal shape of what a probe fact is worth when the host is not exclusively held: not stale-after-a-timeout, but invalidated by the very next effectful step. (3) The escape hatch is the STATE GUARANTEE — a permission rooted at a node of a hierarchical state space guarantees the object cannot leave that subtree even under concurrent modification, so coarse knowledge survives while fine knowledge is surrendered. That is the only graceful-degradation primitive in the round: 'the user still exists' can outlive an unmodelled mutation that destroys 'the user is still in group docker'. Also supplies state DIMENSIONS (orthogonal decompositions, so netns facts need not be invalidated by a filesystem mutation) and fractions as the accounting device permitting a split permission to be rejoined.

A-lifetimes-as-program-points-2017.grading-reasoning: provenance. The normative first-party design document in the official RFC repository — the thing the implementation was built from — not a blog write-up or a retrospective explainer. It is not academically peer-reviewed, which is what would otherwise argue B, but the canonical-first-party-spec clause governs and the document is primary, versioned, and the accepted artifact.
A-lifetimes-as-program-points-2017.relevance-description: The source that most directly licenses P3's reframing, and it corrects it on one point. The whole RFC is the move from 'a lifetime is a lexical region of the AST' to 'a lifetime is a SET OF POINTS in the control-flow graph' — and critically a set that MAY HAVE GAPS, because the same variable can be written, used and rewritten. So an availability window is not an interval; typing it as one silently over-approximates every re-creation, and the RFC records that Rust's EARLIER design required continuous regions and that this is exactly what made one of its problem cases unfixable. Four further transfers: liveness rather than scope is the driver (a window should be driven by whether a LATER command consumes a fact, not by where the creating command sits); location-aware subtyping, with an explicit rejection of both SSA and per-point-types as alternatives — the pre-existing argument against 'just SSA the script'; false edges for non-terminating regions, the same hazard Dorc has with supervisor loops and exec; and may_dangle, a two-track liveness where DESTRUCTION requires weaker freshness than use. Its appendix on what could not be fixed is unusually candid and all three failures are cross-procedural, the middle one — disjoint fields inexpressible across a function boundary, fixed by refactoring the signature so disjointness is visible at the call site — being the same shape as requiring an oracle to declare which contexts it touches rather than taking the host wholesale.

A-definite-assignment-syntactic-conserva.grading-reasoning: primary-vs-secondary. This is the normative text itself — the rules a conforming compiler must implement, not a description of them. Nothing about a language specification published by its own steward argues for B here.
A-definite-assignment-syntactic-conserva.relevance-description: Answers why a position-indexed availability analysis should be SYNTACTIC, and the reason is not tractability — it is that the analysis must be identically decidable by every conforming implementation. A rule of the form 'reject unless you can prove it' makes the accept/reject boundary a property of the TOOLCHAIN rather than of the language, so the same program compiles under one compiler and fails under another. Read onto Dorc: an analyzer whose acceptance set drifts with its own improvements is one whose users cannot write portable books. Also supplies the judgement shape (four position-relative predicates, split into after-when-true and after-when-false for boolean expressions, so flow-sensitivity survives without consulting values), a four-valued lattice whose fourth cell — definitely-assigned AND definitely-unassigned — is reserved for unreachable code, which 28Q's `never` cell should be checked against. Its loop rule breaks the naive circularity with a HYPOTHETICAL judgement (assume, then discharge) rather than a fixpoint over iterations — the move any 'this context survives the loop' rule will need. And it states its own over-rejections outright, including the uncorrelated-guards case that is a Dorc book's daily bread.
